FN-848JE22-1
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 110
Committee: Public Safety and Homeland Sponsor: Representative Ontario Tillman
Security
Analyst: Peter Grogan Date: 01/20/2026
House Bill 110 as introduced would increase the obligations of the Alabama Law Enforcement
Agency (ALEA) by an undetermined amount to develop and implement a digital driver license
and nondriver identification card, which could be offset in whole or in part, dependent upon the
number of digital licenses or ids issued and the $15 fee charged by ALEA pursuant to the
provisions of this bill.
Page 1

FN-848JE22-2
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 110
Committee: Public Safety and Homeland Sponsor: Representative Ontario Tillman
Security
Analyst: Peter Grogan Date: 01/21/2026
House Bill 110 as reported by the Committee on Public Safety and Homeland Security would
increase the obligations of the Alabama Law Enforcement Agency (ALEA) by an undetermined
amount to develop and implement a digital driver license and nondriver identification card,
which could be offset in whole or in part, dependent upon the number of digital licenses or ids
issued and the $15 fee charged by ALEA pursuant to the provisions of this bill.
The provisions of this bill are contingent upon the availability of funding.

Committee: State Governmental Affairs Sponsor: Representative Ontario Tillman

House Bill 110 as passed the House of Representatives would increase the obligations of the
Alabama Law Enforcement Agency (ALEA) by an undetermined amount to develop and
implement a digital driver license and nondriver identification card, which could be offset in
whole or in part, dependent upon the number of digital licenses or IDs issued and the $15 fee
charged by ALEA pursuant to the provisions of this bill.
The provisions of this bill are contingent upon the availability of funding.

FN-848JE22-4
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 110
Committee: State Governmental Affairs Sponsor: Representative Ontario Tillman
Analyst: Peter Grogan Date: 02/04/2026
House Bill 110 as reported by the Committee on State Governmental Affairs would increase the
obligations of the Alabama Law Enforcement Agency (ALEA) by an undetermined amount to
develop and implement a digital driver license and nondriver identification card, which could be
offset in whole or in part, dependent upon the number of digital licenses or IDs issued and the
$15 fee charged by ALEA and deposited into the Public Safety Fund, pursuant to the provisions
of this bill.
The provisions of this bill are contingent upon the availability of funding.
